correctness.rationale: For each full-rank two-column real input, the two possible original-column projection errors have the exact ratio t². The Gaussian sketched-norm decision is the sign of a two-dimensional indefinite quadratic form summed independently across sketch rows. Its positive/negative eigenvalues yield an exact ratio of independent chi-square variables and a symmetric beta CDF. Explicit monotonicity proves orthogonality is worst; beta-density comparison gives the sharp k=2 uniform threshold; the k=4 rational derivative gives its unique sharp extremum; small-beta asymptotics give all high-contrast limits. No finite simulation is used as proof. verify.py passed 1,316 supplementary diagnostic assertions.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural two-column minimum case of Gaussian-sketched QRCP and asks for a global, expected original-column projection-loss calibration, rather than a preset arbitrary example. It establishes a sharp qualitative threshold (one sketch row has unbounded input-uniform mean loss, two suffice for universal ceiling two), an attained sharp four-row constant, and exact all-geometry failure rates. These quantify oversampling design and expose a distinction between high-probability reliability and rare-event expected approximation quality; the finite case serves as an exact algorithm benchmark.
